pathway.title: Mercer International Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Liquidity and refinancing are the weakest dimension and set the timetable. Cash plus undrawn facilities fell to USD 143,531 thousand from USD 488,582 thousand at FY2024, and USD 72,524 thousand of that is undrawn capacity that includes a letters-of-credit-only line and German availability that exists only under the waiver's utilization cap. The Canadian Facility, USD 72,594 thousand drawn, matures in January 2027 and the German Facility, USD 267,837 thousand drawn, in September 2027, together USD 340,431 thousand, and the German leverage covenant is tested again at 2026-12-31. A miss could let the German lenders accelerate and cross-default the notes, so the bank facilities cannot be assumed to stay available to maturity. Basis: calculation B3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 11, 13, 44

Earnings are negative and the third-quarter improvement is not durable. Operating EBITDA was negative USD 36,145 thousand over the last twelve months, so cash interest of USD 110,562 thousand is uncovered, with cover at negative 0.33x against 2.31x in FY2024. Third-quarter Operating EBITDA improved by USD 25,226 thousand year on year, but a grant of USD 12,968 thousand and a smaller inventory write-down explain it; like for like, the quarter was negative USD 7,819 thousand against negative USD 7,677 thousand a year earlier (Analyst Judgement). Basis: calculation B1; calculation B5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The operating franchise is the main support, but it is not low-cost enough to carry the debt at current prices. Mercer has four kraft mills that the issuer describes as modern, surplus energy sales and no customer above 10% of revenue, and the pulp segment returned to a Segment Operating EBITDA of USD 5,890 thousand in the third quarter. Pulp products were 69.85% of FY2025 revenue and each USD 10 per tonne of realization is worth about USD 18,299 thousand a year on FY2025 volumes, about half of the trailing loss, so the franchise supports recovery only if prices or fiber costs turn. Basis: calculation B7; calculation B8; calculation B11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 31

The restructuring plan is the strongest near-term support and also the largest unknown. Noteholders holding about 87% of the notes and holders of about half the equity back a prepackaged plan that would repay the German Facility, add an asset-based facility of up to USD 300,000 thousand and raise USD 400,000 thousand of new cash through a backstopped rights offering. The plan is not confirmed, the chapter 11 cases had not started at 2026-11-05, and its effect on leverage is not established because no pro forma net debt is stated. Basis: calculation B12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 7, 8, 12, 51

Cash conversion is negative even after capital spending was cut. Operating cash flow after interest was negative USD 74,618 thousand over the last twelve months and free cash flow was negative USD 127,445 thousand, with nine-month capital spending of USD 38,674 thousand against USD 74,430 thousand and inventories absorbing USD 85,201 thousand. The cash burn is therefore operational and not only a capital-spending choice. Basis: calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 6

Governance and financial policy are a medium risk that does not change the view. Mercer has no sponsor, paid dividends of USD 10,039 thousand in 2025 before suspending the dividend on 2025-07-31, and no priming, uptier or fee leakage is documented. Board and holder detail was not supplied, so this dimension stays provisional. Basis: calculation B13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: Mercer's first strength is an energy-integrated pulp system that the issuer describes as modern. Four kraft mills with cogeneration sold surplus energy and chemicals worth USD 81,857 thousand in FY2025, which lowers unit cost against older mills and gives a revenue line unrelated to pulp prices; the weakness of this support is its size, about 4.38% of revenue. Basis: calculation B7; calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 9

A second strength is breadth of customers and geography: no customer exceeded 10% of revenue and sales are split across Germany, China and the United States, so a single customer loss is unlikely to threaten debt service, although all regions are exposed to the same global price. Basis: calculation B7; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 124, 128

A third strength is creditor support for the restructuring: noteholders holding about 87% of the notes have agreed to a plan that would put USD 400,000 thousand of new cash into the company and replace the 2027 bank maturities, which makes a negotiated outcome more likely than a disorderly default, but only if the court confirms the plan. Basis: calculation B12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 7, 8, 12

The first weakness is liquidity against maturities: USD 143,531 thousand of liquidity faces USD 340,431 thousand of facility maturities in 2027 and a covenant test at 2026-12-31, so refinancing cannot be done from internal resources and depends on the plan or a new waiver. Basis: calculation B3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 13, 43, 44

The second weakness is negative earnings and cash flow: Operating EBITDA of negative USD 36,145 thousand and free cash flow of negative USD 127,445 thousand over twelve months mean interest is paid from the cash balance and revolver, which cannot continue for long; the third-quarter gain does not change this. Basis: calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The third weakness is exposure to prices and fiber costs Mercer does not set: about 55% of pulp cash cost is fiber and each USD 10 per tonne of realization is worth about USD 18,299 thousand a year, so a small price move changes the debt service picture materially. Basis: calculation B8; calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 19

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The central transaction is the prepackaged restructuring under the support agreements signed on 2026-11-02. Mercer and one non-operating subsidiary intend to file chapter 11 cases in the Southern District of Texas; the operating subsidiaries are not filing and the company expects to complete the restructuring by the end of 2026. Senior noteholders holding about 87% of the notes principal and holders of about 50% of the common stock have agreed to vote for the plan. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 7, 8, 12

Under the plan, holders of the USD 400,000 thousand 2028 notes and USD 875,000 thousand 2029 notes would receive 91.5% of the new common stock, 56.5% of USD 325,000 thousand of new convertible preferred stock and USD 150,000 thousand of takeback senior secured notes, plus the right to join a rights offering of USD 420,000 thousand of new senior secured notes for USD 400,000 thousand of cash, fully backstopped by members of an ad hoc group. The terms also include put option notes of USD 56,000 thousand, linked to a put option premium that the summary does not describe further. All new secured notes would sit under one indenture, mature four years and 364 days after issue and have no scheduled amortization, with interest payable in kind at the issuer's option for the first two years. Basis: calculation A9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 8, 12

Existing common stock would be cancelled, and holders would receive 8.5% of the new common stock and 3.5% of the new convertible preferred stock. On the effective date Mercer would enter a new asset-based revolving facility of up to USD 300,000 thousand, repay and terminate the German Facility and cut the Canadian Facility by at least USD 41,000 thousand, subject to any amendment extending its maturity by five years. Trade and other general unsecured creditors would be unimpaired. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 8, 12, 43

The earlier debt actions are smaller. In October 2024 Mercer added USD 200,000 thousand of 12.875% notes due 2028 at 103.000% of principal and redeemed USD 300,000 thousand of notes due January 2026. In 2026 it obtained a waiver of the German Facility leverage covenant dated 2026-05-04, did not pay about USD 25,800 thousand of interest on the 2028 notes due 2026-10-01, and obtained majority consent on 2026-10-30 to lengthen the grace period from 30 days to 90 days. Government support for the Peace River mill in August 2026 comprised C$18.1 million of grants and a repayable contribution of up to C$19.0 million. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 9, 12, 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Mercer International Inc. (issuer id merc-1333274) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway, covering the consolidated group's statements, debt, liquidity and leverage. The scope is the five supplied annual and quarterly reports and the Source readiness output of this run; no market, rating, peer or legal-document inputs were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer's leverage and interest cover cannot be measured on current earnings: trailing twelve-month Operating EBITDA to 2026-09-30 is negative USD 36,145 thousand, so creditors are relying on the planned chapter 11 restructuring and not on cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 1,593,466 thousand at 2026-09-30, or USD 1,588,380 thousand pro forma for grant funds received in October 2026, against USD 1,298,476 thousand at the end of FY2024, when leverage was 6.09x on Operating EBITDA of USD 243,722 thousand. Cash fell to USD 71,007 thousand and undrawn facilities were USD 72,524 thousand, against USD 340,431 thousand of facility maturities in 2027. The Q3 gain in Operating EBITDA to negative USD 2,851 thousand includes a government grant of USD 12,968 thousand and is not a recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage was already elevated when earnings were positive. At FY2024 carrying debt of USD 1,483,401 thousand was 6.09x Operating EBITDA of USD 243,722 thousand, and net leverage was 5.33x after cash of USD 184,925 thousand. The issuer's definition adds back the goodwill write-off and the loss on the joint venture disposal, USD 57,922 thousand together; on operating income plus depreciation alone the FY2024 ratio would have been 7.98x, so 6.09x is the favourable reading. From FY2025 the measure fails: Operating EBITDA was negative USD 22,019 thousand and the twelve months to 2026-09-30 were negative USD 36,145 thousand, while debt rose to USD 1,664,473 thousand. Creditors can no longer size the debt against earnings, and it is being carried by the cash balance, revolver draws and now the restructuring.

fields.value: Cash interest paid was USD 110,562 thousand over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 against negative Operating EBITDA, so EBITDA cover was negative 0.33x, compared with 2.31x in FY2024 and negative 0.20x in FY2025. The senior notes alone carry cash coupons of USD 96,343.75 thousand a year, and cash of USD 71,007 thousand covers 0.74x of one year of those coupons. The 2028 notes coupon of about USD 25,800 thousand due 2026-10-01 was not paid, and on 2026-10-30 the grace period was lengthened from 30 days to 90 days, which on a count from the due date runs to 2026-12-30. Interest is therefore being paid or deferred out of liquidity and not out of earnings, and the extended grace period makes late December the first dated test of the restructuring timetable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is the third quarter: Operating EBITDA improved by USD 25,226 thousand year on year to negative USD 2,851 thousand, and capital spending was cut. The improvement is explained by two items and not by operations: a government grant of USD 12,968 thousand credited to cost of sales, and a smaller inventory write-down, USD 8,000 thousand against USD 20,400 thousand a year earlier. Adding back the write-downs and removing the grant gives negative USD 7,819 thousand against negative USD 7,677 thousand a year earlier, an unchanged run rate (Analyst Judgement, not an issuer measure; inventory write-downs recurred in every year shown, so the reported figure stays the denominator). The view would improve with two consecutive quarters of positive Operating EBITDA that include no grant and write-downs at or below the third-quarter level, and with the German Facility, whose margin was raised to a range of 2.50% to 4.25% under the waiver, repaid under the plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow shows that the earnings problem is a cash problem. Operating cash flow, which is after cash interest, was negative USD 74,618 thousand over the twelve months to 2026-09-30, and after capital spending of USD 52,827 thousand free cash flow was negative USD 127,445 thousand; in FY2024 it was positive USD 5,886 thousand. FY2025 operating cash flow of USD 8,587 thousand was positive only after a receivables release of USD 52,588 thousand, and in the nine months of 2026 the inventory build absorbed USD 85,201 thousand even though USD 59,000 thousand of inventory was written down. Nine-month capital spending was cut 48.04% to USD 38,674 thousand, which flatters free cash flow: the sources give no maintenance and growth split, so how much of the cut is deferral is not established.

fields.value: The nine-month outflow was met from cash and borrowing. Cash and restricted cash fell by USD 110,798 thousand, revolving facilities were drawn for USD 55,675 thousand net and the new repayable government contribution added USD 6,034 thousand; dividends stopped after USD 10,039 thousand was paid in 2025, when Operating EBITDA was already negative. Customer deposits for mass timber contracts, a small non-debt funding source, fell from USD 16,434 thousand at FY2025 to USD 10,446 thousand, a drop of 36.44%, which removes a further source of working capital as projects complete. The pattern is a business drawing down its remaining facility headroom to fund working capital and interest, which is why the maturity profile in the next section matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the third quarter revenue fell 3.80% to USD 440,668 thousand on lower pulp volumes and realizations, with softwood pulp realizations at USD 671 per tonne against USD 728 a year earlier. Interest expense rose 13.39% to USD 32,323 thousand, reflecting higher borrowings and the higher German Facility margin under the waiver, and operating cash flow was negative USD 19,992 thousand. The fourth quarter opened with a further cost: the Rosenthal mill lost 24 days to unplanned downtime after its annual maintenance, which the quarterly report states without quantifying the earnings effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the binding constraint. Cash plus undrawn facilities fell from USD 488,582 thousand at FY2024 to USD 430,364 thousand at FY2025 and USD 143,531 thousand at 2026-09-30, which is 8.62% of carrying debt against 32.94% at FY2024. The USD 72,524 thousand of undrawn capacity is flattered in three ways: USD 6,962 thousand is a letters-of-credit-only line that cannot fund cash needs, the German Facility availability of USD 48,655 thousand exists only after the waiver caps utilization at EUR 300.0 million while German leverage exceeds 2.00x, and USD 5,000 thousand of cash is restricted collateral and is excluded from the cash figure. The waiver also requires average liquidity of at least USD 30,000 thousand, tested monthly over a rolling 13-week period, so the headroom over that floor is USD 113,531 thousand at the quarter end (Analyst Judgement).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2027 maturities exceed liquidity. The Canadian Facility, USD 72,594 thousand drawn, falls due in January 2027 and the German Facility, USD 267,837 thousand drawn, in September 2027, together USD 340,431 thousand against liquidity of USD 143,531 thousand, a shortfall of USD 196,900 thousand; both were classified as current at 2026-09-30, lifting current debt to USD 354,703 thousand. The senior notes then fall due in October 2028, USD 400,000 thousand, and February 2029, USD 875,000 thousand. Management stated in the second-quarter report that it was probable the German leverage covenant would not be met at 2026-12-31, when testing resumes, and an unwaived breach could lead to acceleration and cross-defaults, so the facilities cannot be assumed to stay available to their maturity. Under the restructuring support agreements the German Facility would be repaid and terminated, the Canadian Facility reduced by at least USD 41,000 thousand, a new asset-based facility of up to USD 300,000 thousand put in place and USD 400,000 thousand of new money raised through the rights offering, none of which is in the 2026-09-30 balance sheet.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contrary evidence is that the plan leaves general unsecured creditors unimpaired and holders of about 87% of the senior notes principal have signed support agreements, so the near-term outcome points to a negotiated deleveraging and not a disorderly default, while cash of USD 71,007 thousand and undrawn capacity of USD 72,524 thousand cover ordinary-course obligations on the issuer's own statement. What would change the view is the filing of the chapter 11 cases and court approval of the rights offering and the new asset-based facility; until then the sources do not establish the petition date, any debtor-in-possession financing or the outcome of the extended interest grace period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The statements are consolidated for Mercer International Inc. and all its subsidiaries, but the senior notes are the parent's unsecured obligations and are not guaranteed by the operating subsidiaries that own the mills. The notes therefore rank behind secured debt and all subsidiary debt and liabilities, including the Canadian Facility, which has a first-priority charge over substantially all borrower assets, and the German Facility, whose waiver provides for security over certain German assets. Consolidated cash and facility figures overstate what is available at the parent, because the waiver barred distributions from the German borrowers to the parent until 2026-09-30 with limited exceptions, and no parent-only statements were supplied to size the gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three definitions drive the figures. Operating EBITDA is the issuer's own non-GAAP measure and the only EBITDA it states; it adds back long-lived asset impairments, USD 215,682 thousand in FY2025 and USD 57,922 thousand of impairment and disposal items in FY2024, but not inventory write-downs, which were USD 54,400 thousand in FY2025 and USD 59,000 thousand in the nine months of 2026 and stay in the figure. Total debt is carrying value including the finance lease liability of USD 48,203 thousand that the issuer carries in its debt lines, while operating lease liabilities of USD 5,731 thousand are separate and excluded. The issuer's available-capacity figure of USD 72,524 thousand is used as stated for liquidity even though it includes a letters-of-credit-only line.

fields.value: Five events after 2026-09-30 are shown beside and not inside the period figures: the 2028 notes coupon not paid on 2026-10-01, the second supplemental indenture of 2026-10-30 extending the grace period, receipt in October 2026 of USD 5,086 thousand of the Peace River grant, the restructuring support agreements of 2026-11-02, and an unplanned 24-day outage at the Rosenthal mill in the fourth quarter. Only the grant receipt changes net debt on a stated amount, giving pro forma net debt of USD 1,588,380 thousand; the support agreements are conditional on court confirmation, so no pro forma figure is stated for them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Four presentation differences need care. The current finance lease liability sits in accounts payable and other in the annual reports and in current debt in the quarterly reports; the FY2024 joint venture investment is folded into other long-term assets in the FY2025 report; the German Facility is non-current at 2026-03-31 and current at the two later quarter ends; and cash in the interim cash flow statements includes restricted cash. Each is shown as filed with the other presentation beside it, and none changes a total. Items the sources do not state, namely interest income, a maintenance and growth capex split, an adjusted EBITDA, parent-only statements and the discrete first and second quarter flows, are listed under Gaps and are not estimated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for Mercer International Inc. (issuer id merc-1333274) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway, covering the business, ownership, transactions, history and governance behavior relevant to creditors. The scope is the five supplied annual and quarterly reports and the Source readiness output of this run; no sponsor, market or legal-document inputs were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer has no sponsor to inject equity, so creditor protection rests on its own capital allocation and on a restructuring in which senior noteholders holding about 87% of the notes would receive most of the reorganized equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A1; calculation A9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 7, 8, 12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a commodity pulp and lumber producer: pulp was 69.85% of FY2025 revenue and fiber about 55% of pulp cash cost, which ties earnings to prices Mercer does not set. Governance evidence is mixed rather than adverse: dividends of USD 10,039 thousand were paid in 2025, a year in which Operating EBITDA was negative, and were then suspended on 2025-07-31, and no uptier, priming or fee leakage is documented. Board and shareholder detail was not supplied, so the governance conclusion is provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A2; calculation A8; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 19, 57, 63, 124; 10-K_2024-12-31_2024-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control is dispersed and unquantified, so no sponsor support should be assumed. The annual report says a few significant shareholders own a substantial percentage of the shares and can influence elections and major transactions, but no holder or percentage is named in the supplied reports. The only disclosed shareholder-linked commercial tie is a surety bond facility of up to USD 30,000 thousand with an entity owned by a major shareholder, on standard commercial premiums and nominally used. Creditors therefore cannot rely on a parent or fund to cure a shortfall, and the only new money now offered comes from the noteholders themselves.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation was growth-led and then defensive, with mixed creditor impact. Since 2021 Mercer invested about USD 396.6 million to widen solid wood, including the Torgau facility in 2022 for about USD 263.2 million and the Conway and Okanagan facilities in 2023 for about USD 82.1 million, while the funding mix of those purchases is not stated in the supplied reports. It also paid dividends of USD 10,039 thousand in 2025 when operating cash flow of USD 8,587 thousand did not cover them, then suspended the dividend and cut nine-month capital spending to USD 38,674 thousand from USD 74,430 thousand. The pattern shows dividends continuing into a year in which Operating EBITDA ended negative, which is a modest early-warning signal for creditors, offset by the suspension in July 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is cyclical and fiber-dependent, with energy sales a small cushion. Pulp products were 69.85% of FY2025 revenue and fiber was about 55% of pulp cash production cost and 75% of lumber cash cost, so a rise in fiber prices or a fall in pulp prices hits margins directly; surplus energy and chemicals in the pulp segment were 4.38% of revenue. Sales are spread across Germany at 25.44%, China at 29.45% and the United States at 16.00% of FY2025 revenue, and no customer exceeded 10% of revenue, so concentration is low but price exposure is global.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A2; calculation A4; calculation A7; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 9, 19, 124, 128

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The restructuring is creditor-led in direction but untested. Under the support agreements senior noteholders would receive 91.5% of the new common stock, 56.5% of the new convertible preferred stock and USD 150,000 thousand of takeback notes, and could take part in a rights offering of USD 420,000 thousand of new senior secured notes backstopped by an ad hoc group, while existing holders would keep 8.5% of the new common stock. The existing holders' 8.5% is diluted only by the management incentive plan and by conversion of the preferred stock, whereas the noteholders' 91.5% is also diluted by the rights offering stock, a term that favours the equity class relative to the noteholders (Analyst Interpretation). Existing equity keeping a protected residual stake while the senior notes are impaired is a point creditors should test against the executed documents, which were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for financial monitoring and thin for governance. The FY2025 audit opinion was unqualified with effective internal control, and the interim reports give facility availability, covenant status and waiver terms; but board composition, committee independence, pay and related-party review are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that was not supplied, and the ownership share of a logging and chipping operation is stated as 50% in the FY2024 report and 20% in the FY2025 report without explanation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against reading the outcome as creditor-led is that the plan is conditional on court confirmation and that holders of about half of the common stock, whose claims rank behind notes that the issuer's own fair value disclosure puts at 29.06% of principal, are party to the agreements and keep a residual stake. If the executed documents show releases for shareholders, a management incentive plan that dilutes the noteholders' 91.5%, or consent terms that favour consenting holders over the rest, the alignment view would weaken. In the other direction, governance behaviour has been more cautious than the business's leverage suggests: the dividend was suspended in July 2025, the waiver bars distributions to the parent until 2026-09-30, and general unsecured creditors are unimpaired under the plan. A proxy statement showing a controlling holder, any evidence that the 2025 dividends or the acquisitions were debt-funded against creditor interests, or a plan outcome on different terms after 2026-11-05 would change the view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation A9; calculation A15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 8, 12, 13, 26, 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, page 57

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, holder names and ownership percentages are not established; this limits the conclusion that no holder controls Mercer and makes the governance view provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed indentures, waiver letter and restructuring support agreements were not supplied, so what the documents permit for distributions and how equity and noteholders are treated rest on the issuer's summaries; this limits the creditor-alignment conclusion and the view of legal capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document dated after 2026-11-05 was supplied, so the petition date, any debtor-in-possession financing and the outcome of the extended interest grace period are not established; this limits whether the restructuring timetable behind the view still holds at the cutoff.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The 2022 and 2023 annual reports were not supplied, so how the Torgau, Conway and Okanagan acquisitions were funded is not established; this limits the conclusion that growth was debt-funded and the reading of financial policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers below follow the method's order; each is a table with its own source column.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The central transaction is the prepackaged restructuring under the support agreements signed on 2026-11-02. Mercer and one non-operating subsidiary intend to file chapter 11 cases in the Southern District of Texas; the operating subsidiaries are not filing and the company expects to complete the restructuring by the end of 2026. Senior noteholders holding about 87% of the notes principal and holders of about 50% of the common stock have agreed to vote for the plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Under the plan, holders of the USD 400,000 thousand 2028 notes and USD 875,000 thousand 2029 notes would receive 91.5% of the new common stock, 56.5% of USD 325,000 thousand of new convertible preferred stock and USD 150,000 thousand of takeback senior secured notes, plus the right to join a rights offering of USD 420,000 thousand of new senior secured notes for USD 400,000 thousand of cash, fully backstopped by members of an ad hoc group. The terms also include put option notes of USD 56,000 thousand, linked to a put option premium that the summary does not describe further. All new secured notes would sit under one indenture, mature four years and 364 days after issue and have no scheduled amortization, with interest payable in kind at the issuer's option for the first two years.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Existing common stock would be cancelled, and holders would receive 8.5% of the new common stock and 3.5% of the new convertible preferred stock. On the effective date Mercer would enter a new asset-based revolving facility of up to USD 300,000 thousand, repay and terminate the German Facility and cut the Canadian Facility by at least USD 41,000 thousand, subject to any amendment extending its maturity by five years. Trade and other general unsecured creditors would be unimpaired.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earlier debt actions are smaller. In October 2024 Mercer added USD 200,000 thousand of 12.875% notes due 2028 at 103.000% of principal and redeemed USD 300,000 thousand of notes due January 2026. In 2026 it obtained a waiver of the German Facility leverage covenant dated 2026-05-04, did not pay about USD 25,800 thousand of interest on the 2028 notes due 2026-10-01, and obtained majority consent on 2026-10-30 to lengthen the grace period from 30 days to 90 days. Government support for the Peace River mill in August 2026 comprised C$18.1 million of grants and a repayable contribution of up to C$19.0 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Mercer presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behavior is a dividend of USD 10,039 thousand paid in 2025 and suspended on 2025-07-31, followed by a covenant waiver, a deferred coupon and a noteholder-led restructuring plan, which matters because cash left while liquidity tightened and now creditors rather than a sponsor decide the outcome. Countervailing evidence is the absence of a sponsor, no documented priming, uptier or fee leakage, and unimpaired general unsecured creditors. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed agreements and any filings after 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The governance review is completed with limitations. Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. Key gaps: board and shareholder detail, executed legal documents and events after 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit assessment of Mercer International Inc. (issuer id merc-1333274) as of 2026-11-18 on the credit snapshot pathway, covering business risk, financial profile, liquidity, downside and monitoring. The scope is the five supplied annual and quarterly reports and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance outputs of this run.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer is a distressed credit whose debt can no longer be serviced from earnings, so creditor outcomes depend on the noteholder-led restructuring and not on the operating business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Trailing twelve-month Operating EBITDA is negative USD 36,145 thousand against cash interest paid of USD 110,562 thousand, and net debt is USD 1,593,466 thousand at 2026-09-30, or USD 1,588,380 thousand pro forma for grant funds received in October 2026. Liquidity of USD 143,531 thousand compares with USD 340,431 thousand of facility maturities in 2027 and a covenant test on 2026-12-31 that management said in the second-quarter report it was probable the company would fail. The issuer describes its mills as modern and they sell surplus energy, and noteholders holding about 87% of the notes have backed a plan with USD 400,000 thousand of new cash, but the plan is unconfirmed and nothing after 2026-11-05 is established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B2; calculation B3; calculation B12; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-06-30_Q2-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 8, 12, 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and refinancing are the weakest dimension and set the timetable. Cash plus undrawn facilities fell to USD 143,531 thousand from USD 488,582 thousand at FY2024, and USD 72,524 thousand of that is undrawn capacity that includes a letters-of-credit-only line and German availability that exists only under the waiver's utilization cap. The Canadian Facility, USD 72,594 thousand drawn, matures in January 2027 and the German Facility, USD 267,837 thousand drawn, in September 2027, together USD 340,431 thousand, and the German leverage covenant is tested again at 2026-12-31. A miss could let the German lenders accelerate and cross-default the notes, so the bank facilities cannot be assumed to stay available to maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 11, 13, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are negative and the third-quarter improvement is not durable. Operating EBITDA was negative USD 36,145 thousand over the last twelve months, so cash interest of USD 110,562 thousand is uncovered, with cover at negative 0.33x against 2.31x in FY2024. Third-quarter Operating EBITDA improved by USD 25,226 thousand year on year, but a grant of USD 12,968 thousand and a smaller inventory write-down explain it; like for like, the quarter was negative USD 7,819 thousand against negative USD 7,677 thousand a year earlier (Analyst Judgement).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B5; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating franchise is the main support, but it is not low-cost enough to carry the debt at current prices. Mercer has four kraft mills that the issuer describes as modern, surplus energy sales and no customer above 10% of revenue, and the pulp segment returned to a Segment Operating EBITDA of USD 5,890 thousand in the third quarter. Pulp products were 69.85% of FY2025 revenue and each USD 10 per tonne of realization is worth about USD 18,299 thousand a year on FY2025 volumes, about half of the trailing loss, so the franchise supports recovery only if prices or fiber costs turn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B7; calculation B8; calculation B11; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 31

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The restructuring plan is the strongest near-term support and also the largest unknown. Noteholders holding about 87% of the notes and holders of about half the equity back a prepackaged plan that would repay the German Facility, add an asset-based facility of up to USD 300,000 thousand and raise USD 400,000 thousand of new cash through a backstopped rights offering. The plan is not confirmed, the chapter 11 cases had not started at 2026-11-05, and its effect on leverage is not established because no pro forma net debt is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B12; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 7, 8, 12, 51

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is negative even after capital spending was cut. Operating cash flow after interest was negative USD 74,618 thousand over the last twelve months and free cash flow was negative USD 127,445 thousand, with nine-month capital spending of USD 38,674 thousand against USD 74,430 thousand and inventories absorbing USD 85,201 thousand. The cash burn is therefore operational and not only a capital-spending choice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance and financial policy are a medium risk that does not change the view. Mercer has no sponsor, paid dividends of USD 10,039 thousand in 2025 before suspending the dividend on 2025-07-31, and no priming, uptier or fee leakage is documented. Board and holder detail was not supplied, so this dimension stays provisional.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a distressed view is operating stabilisation. Third-quarter revenue fell only 3.80%, the pulp segment returned to USD 5,890 thousand of Segment Operating EBITDA from negative USD 12,686 thousand, solid wood revenue rose 9.73%, per unit fiber costs at the Canadian mills are expected to fall after Celgar's supply contracts were renegotiated, and the issuer expects NBSK prices to rise modestly in the fourth quarter. Liquidity of USD 143,531 thousand also exceeds the waiver's minimum of USD 30,000 thousand by USD 113,531 thousand, so cash is not yet exhausted. The view would soften if the plan is confirmed on the stated terms and removes the 2027 bank maturities, or if two quarters of positive Operating EBITDA without grants follow; it would harden if the covenant test at 2026-12-31 is missed without relief, if the plan terms change after 2026-11-05, or if German fiber costs rise while pulp prices stay flat.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B7; calculation B11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 3, 29, 30, 31, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No management projections or covenant compliance calculations were supplied, so the downside path and the December 2026 covenant test rest on reported results and the issuer's own statement that a breach is probable; this limits how precisely the timing of a liquidity shortfall can be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sources give no pulp price or fiber cost sensitivities, so the earnings effect of a price or cost move is shown as arithmetic on reported volumes and not as a forecast; this limits the downside scenario to a direction and a sequence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No market quotes, independent rating reports or peer data were supplied and the ratings are the issuer's own account, so Mercer is not compared with other leveraged issuers; this limits any statement of relative standing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The exit capital structure is known only from the summary of the support agreements and no pro forma net debt is stated, so leverage after emergence is not established; this limits the post-restructuring credit conclusion to the stated sources of new cash and the removal of the 2027 bank maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sections and registers below follow the method's steps; each table carries its own source column.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer International Inc. is a Washington corporation headquartered in Vancouver that runs two segments from sites in Germany, Canada and the United States: pulp, with four kraft mills of about 2.1 million tonnes a year of capacity, 86% of it softwood grade, and solid wood, with sawmills, pallet and biofuel plants and mass timber plants. In FY2025 pulp products were 69.85% of revenue, lumber 13.25%, energy and chemicals 5.81% and pallets 5.36%, and Germany, China and the United States took 25.44%, 29.45% and 16.00% of sales. Mercer is a price-taker with dollar revenue and euro and Canadian dollar costs; the model gives low customer concentration but high cash-flow volatility and little revenue visibility, so debt service capacity depends on the price cycle and not on contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B7; calculation B16; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 7, 8, 124

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer is a listed company with no sponsor, a dispersed shareholder base and a few unnamed significant holders. The senior notes are unsecured parent obligations that the operating subsidiaries do not guarantee, while the subsidiaries that own the mills carry the secured Canadian Facility and the German Facility, so noteholders rank behind subsidiary and secured debt in the current structure and the waiver barred cash distributions from the German borrowers to the parent until 2026-09-30. A sponsor-free structure removes extraction risk but also any equity cure: dividends of USD 10,039 thousand were paid in 2025 and suspended on 2025-07-31, and the only new money now offered comes from the noteholders. Board composition and holder percentages are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B13; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 34, 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is cyclical and price-driven. NBSK realization fell to USD 671 per tonne in the third quarter from USD 728, down 7.83%, nine-month NBSK sales volume fell to 1,096.8 thousand tonnes from 1,135.4 thousand, and third-quarter pulp segment revenue fell 8.52% while solid wood revenue rose 9.73% on higher lumber and mass timber realizations. Pricing power is weak in pulp, where competition is on price; surplus energy and chemicals, 4.38% of FY2025 revenue, are the only stable stream. Revenue is neither contracted nor recurring, so a price fall passes straight to EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fiber is about 55% of pulp cash production cost and about 75% of lumber cash production cost, and German fiber costs rose in 2025 on reduced harvest of beetle-infested wood, so margins depend on a cost Mercer cannot control. Pulp segment fiber expense was USD 507,842 thousand in the nine months of 2026, so a 5% rise adds USD 25,392.1 thousand of cost for nine months (arithmetic, not a forecast). Operating leverage is high because mills carry fixed costs, maintenance is expensed under US GAAP, planned downtime cost about USD 34,100 thousand of Segment Operating EBITDA in the third quarter, and a stronger dollar helped by about USD 5.0 million at the operating level in that quarter. Margins cannot be defended against a price fall without a cost offset; the identified levers are lower Canadian fiber costs and the Torgau cost actions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B9; calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 19, 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 23, 33, 34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is not converting to cash. Operating cash flow after interest was negative USD 74,618 thousand over the last twelve months and free cash flow negative USD 127,445 thousand, with capital spending of USD 52,827 thousand and inventories absorbing USD 85,201 thousand in the nine months of 2026. Capital spending was cut to USD 38,674 thousand from USD 74,430 thousand, which shows flexibility, but the maintenance share is not stated. Cash interest of USD 110,562 thousand is the largest fixed cash call and the senior notes alone carry coupons of USD 96,343.75 thousand a year, so EBITDA would have to rise by USD 146,707 thousand for cash interest to be covered once, and by USD 199,534 thousand to cover cash interest and capital spending together.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B6; calculation B10; calculation B17; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, page 6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and price-based. Mercer's NBSK competitors are large producers in Northern Europe and Canada, pulp is a commodity, and about 2.6 million tonnes of net new hardwood capacity is announced for 2026, which pressures prices and lengthens a downturn for a price-taker. Buyer power is high because customers can blend hardwood into their pulp mix, although strength requirements in tissue and lightweight paper limit substitution of softwood. Supplier power sits with fiber owners and is rising in Germany, where wood is also in demand as an energy source. Entry barriers are high because a pulp mill costs a great deal to build, Stendal having cost about USD 1.1 billion, and substitutes are digital media for printing paper, offset by tissue growth. The net effect is weak pricing power and persistent margin pressure, which is why debt capacity should be sized on trough and not peak earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Three outside factors move credit quality. Currency matters because pulp is priced in dollars while many costs are in euros and Canadian dollars, and no derivatives were outstanding at FY2025, so a weaker dollar raises costs relative to revenue. German energy rules matter because surplus power is sold at regulated rates that expire between 2029 and 2034, which will lower a stable revenue stream. Trade policy matters because weak lumber markets and incremental government duties and tariffs led to sawmill curtailments and closures in 2025, which cut wood chip supply and raised per unit fiber costs at the Canadian pulp mills. Interest rates matter chiefly for lumber and mass timber, whose demand is tied to housing and construction finance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths that support credit: four kraft mills, described by the issuer as modern, with energy cogeneration, which lowers unit cost and adds a stable revenue line; low customer concentration; a pulp segment that earned positive Segment Operating EBITDA in the third quarter; and a noteholder group with a backstopped plan. Weaknesses that constrain it: negative Operating EBITDA and uncovered interest; liquidity below the 2027 bank maturities; pulp products at about seventy percent of revenue with prices outside Mercer's control; and unsecured parent notes behind subsidiary debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B7; calculation B11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit: confirmation of the plan with new money and a new asset-based facility; a modest NBSK price rise expected in the fourth quarter of 2026; lower Canadian fiber costs; and public support at the Peace River mill. Threats that could weaken it: a missed covenant test at 2026-12-31; failure to confirm the plan, which the issuer says could lead to a non-prepackaged chapter 11 case or liquidation; higher German fiber costs; and new hardwood capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Mercer's first strength is an energy-integrated pulp system that the issuer describes as modern. Four kraft mills with cogeneration sold surplus energy and chemicals worth USD 81,857 thousand in FY2025, which lowers unit cost against older mills and gives a revenue line unrelated to pulp prices; the weakness of this support is its size, about 4.38% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B7; calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A second strength is breadth of customers and geography: no customer exceeded 10% of revenue and sales are split across Germany, China and the United States, so a single customer loss is unlikely to threaten debt service, although all regions are exposed to the same global price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A third strength is creditor support for the restructuring: noteholders holding about 87% of the notes have agreed to a plan that would put USD 400,000 thousand of new cash into the company and replace the 2027 bank maturities, which makes a negotiated outcome more likely than a disorderly default, but only if the court confirms the plan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is liquidity against maturities: USD 143,531 thousand of liquidity faces USD 340,431 thousand of facility maturities in 2027 and a covenant test at 2026-12-31, so refinancing cannot be done from internal resources and depends on the plan or a new waiver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 13, 43, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is negative earnings and cash flow: Operating EBITDA of negative USD 36,145 thousand and free cash flow of negative USD 127,445 thousand over twelve months mean interest is paid from the cash balance and revolver, which cannot continue for long; the third-quarter gain does not change this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B1; calculation B5; calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is exposure to prices and fiber costs Mercer does not set: about 55% of pulp cash cost is fiber and each USD 10 per tonne of realization is worth about USD 18,299 thousand a year, so a small price move changes the debt service picture materially.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B8; calculation B16; 10-K_2025-12-31_2025-Annual-Report-on-Form-10-K.pdf, pages 8, 19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position are average: Mercer is a large market pulp producer but a price-taker. Competitive advantage is average: mills that the issuer describes as modern and energy sales help, but the product is a commodity. Business diversification is average: two segments and low customer concentration, offset by pulp products at about seventy percent of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capital spending was cut by 48.04% in nine months and cost actions are under way, but fiber cost cannot be managed. Margin stability is weak: Operating EBITDA moved from USD 243,722 thousand in FY2024 to negative USD 36,145 thousand over twelve months. Free cash flow stability is weak: free cash flow was negative USD 127,445 thousand over twelve months. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is weak: ratings are CCC+, CCC and Ca as reported by the issuer, the notes' fair value is 29.06% of principal, and refinancing now depends on the plan. Liquidity is weak: USD 143,531 thousand against USD 340,431 thousand of 2027 maturities. Financial policy and governance are average: no sponsor, the dividend was suspended in 2025, but board detail is not supplied and the plan leaves existing equity a protected stake.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B4; calculation B6; calculation B15; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 26, 45

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are the asset base, surplus energy sales and creditor backing for the plan; the main constraints are negative earnings, short liquidity and the covenant test. The trend is down: debt rose by USD 294,990 thousand net since FY2024 while cash fell by USD 113,918 thousand. The key missing data points are management projections, covenant calculations and the executed plan documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the next 12 to 24 months the issuer expects to complete the restructuring by the end of 2026, NBSK prices to rise modestly in the fourth quarter, lumber prices to be flat, German fiber costs to rise slightly and Canadian fiber costs to fall. Tailwinds are supply curtailments and closures in the industry, a stronger dollar and the Canadian fiber contracts; headwinds are weak Chinese and European demand, the covenant test at 2026-12-31, the Rosenthal mill outage in the fourth quarter and the Torgau staged workforce reduction to about the second quarter of 2027. If the plan is confirmed, the 2027 bank maturities fall away and the benefit of the tailwinds accrues partly to the new owners; if it is not, the headwinds hit a company with cash of USD 71,007 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the sector headwinds are new hardwood capacity of about 2.6 million tonnes announced for 2026, hardwood substitution in market pulp, and the expiry of German regulated energy rates between 2029 and 2034; the tailwinds are tissue demand in emerging markets and constrained softwood supply. Medium-term credit depends on whether prices recover enough to cover a reduced debt load, which cannot be assessed because the post-plan capital structure is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside is a failed bridge to the plan. The initiating condition is a covenant miss at 2026-12-31 or a delay in plan confirmation beyond the extended coupon grace period, which on a count from the due date runs to 2026-12-30, while NBSK prices stay near USD 1,625 per tonne in Europe and USD 645 per tonne in China and German fiber costs rise. The first operational break is at the German mills, where the waiver cap limits availability to USD 48,655 thousand and the German lenders could accelerate USD 267,837 thousand of borrowings. The financial transmission is that acceleration triggers cross-defaults on the Canadian Facility and the notes, USD 1,275,000 thousand of principal, while cash of USD 71,007 thousand covers only 0.74x of one year of note coupons of USD 96,343.75 thousand. A further USD 10 per tonne fall in pulp realization would cost about USD 18,299 thousand a year and a 5% rise in pulp fiber cost about USD 25,392.1 thousand over nine months, both labelled arithmetic and not a forecast. Management levers are already partly used: the dividend is suspended, capital spending is cut, the coupon grace period is extended and the Torgau cost actions are under way; the plan's USD 400,000 thousand of new money is the remaining lever. Resilience appears insufficient to avoid a liquidity event without the plan or a new waiver. The observable triggers are a covenant notice, a lender default notice, a petition filing and a change in plan terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B8; calculation B9; calculation B10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 11, 13, 29, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Mercer presents a weak business and financial profile that is not fully assessable beyond the restructuring, supported by energy-integrated mills that the issuer describes as modern, broad customers and noteholder backing for a plan, but constrained by negative earnings, uncovered interest and liquidity below the 2027 bank maturities. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow was negative USD 127,445 thousand over twelve months and the third-quarter gain came from a grant and a smaller write-down. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on court confirmation of the plan and on the 2026-12-31 covenant test. The primary downside path is a missed covenant test or a delayed plan that lets the German lenders accelerate and cross-default the notes. Further analysis would require the executed plan documents, post-emergence financial projections, covenant calculations and any filing after 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation B3; calculation B5; calculation B6; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_Q3-2026-Quarterly-Report.pdf, pages 12, 13, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fundamental credit review is completed with limitations. Top risk: a liquidity and covenant failure before the plan is confirmed.
